clue.text: Shrub in far gap in ground

indicators.note: ground is the past participle of grind, so these words are milled down and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A bush planted in a far-off gap in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' after 'Shrub' looks like a link word, but both of the clue's 'in's are part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The frangipani is a tropical flowering shrub or small tree, prized for its scented blossom.

clue.text: Fellow cut lemon

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches

explanation.surface: A man slicing a citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is slang for a dud or failure, something that fails to work or sell.

clue.text: Singer entering recital top-notch

indicators.note: the answer is found going into the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A vocalist joining a first-class recital.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Old man, set employee?

definitions.meaning: an old fellow, a codger, or informally the boss or one's father
on a film set, the chief electrician holds this job title

explanation.surface: An elderly man who works on a set.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for an old chap or a boss, and is also the film-crew title of the head lighting electrician.

clue.text: Two lakes around isle with sun featured in magazine once — a cheesy concoction?

indicators.note: the build-up is shown inside the magazine's name, like an article printed within it

parts.note: Punch was a British humorous weekly, now closed

indicators.note: the two lakes sit either side of the island and sun pieces

parts.note: a lough is an Irish lake
L is the abbreviation for lake
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A geography piece about Irish lakes in an old humorous magazine, oddly ending on cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British satirical weekly that closed in 2002, hence 'once'; a lough is the Irish word for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: This British pub meal is bread, cheese and pickle, so the question mark flags a cheese-based plate as a fair description.

clue.text: Clothing group left around college — change at MIT?

indicators.note: the brand and the left letter go round the abbreviation for college

parts.note: Nike is a sportswear company

explanation.surface: A clothing firm abandoning a college, and a question about money at a US university.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT is an American university, so the 'change' is US coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A US five-cent coin is called a nickel, a piece of small change Americans would use.

clue.text: Fake old instrument lacking weight

indicators.note: the instrument is shown going without the weight letter

parts.note: the shawm is a medieval reed instrument

explanation.surface: A counterfeit antique instrument that is underweight.
explanation.walkthrough: A shawm is a medieval forerunner of the oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fake is a pretence or imitation, a counterfeit.

clue.text: Having obtained height, drag in leg manoeuvring in this?

definitions.text: Having obtained height, drag in leg manoeuvring in this?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so these letters are shifted into new places

explanation.surface: A pilot gains altitude, then manoeuvres against drag in one leg of a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang glider is the light unpowered craft in which a pilot rides air currents to gain height and steer.

clue.text: Mad minister, not one for broadcast TV programme

indicators.note: not one says that the letter for one is left out of the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crazy government minister on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an I from MADMINISTER and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz show with a famous black chair.

clue.text: Not communicating but in play presumably?

definitions.meaning: having lost contact, no longer in touch with others
in football or rugby, a ball not over the touchline is still in play

explanation.surface: Someone silent who is nevertheless playing on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lacking contact or current knowledge, and literally describes a ball that is not in the touch area beyond the sideline.

clue.text: Extra amount after book is brought out a burden

indicators.note: the book letter is taken out of the extra payment

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment

explanation.surface: An extra payment after a book is published turns out to be a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' suggests publication of the book, but it means the B is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty, a responsibility one must carry.

clue.text: Malfunctioning — not like regulars in bunch at work?

indicators.note: the letters are set to work, moved around into a new order
the regular letters, first, third and fifth, are taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Something broken down, unlike the regular gang at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars in' picks B, N and H from 'bunch'. These join NOTLIKE, and 'at work' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a machine that is faulty or working only intermittently.

clue.text: Fairylike creature lacking energy, singer and temperamental type?

indicators.note: the fairy figure goes without the energy letter

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
E is the symbol for energy
Madonna is the pop star

explanation.surface: A fairy, a singer, and a moody person listed together.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy-like being in Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a vain, temperamental person, from the leading female singer in an opera.

clue.text: Around end of table, large figure put back pastry

indicators.note: the word for large goes round the end letter of table

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows
the number is written backwards

parts.note: ten is a figure

explanation.surface: A big number placed back around the end of a table, with pastry thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large figure' looks like one piece but is two separate words, and only the figure is put back.
explanation.definitionFit: A beignet is a French fritter, a deep-fried pastry dusted with sugar.

clue.text: Comic character with gossip overturned cushion

parts.note: Mr Bean is the comic TV character

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the word is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: gab is chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: A comedian and a chatterbox knock over a cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large floppy cushion filled with beads, used as a seat.

clue.text: Occupation of property in outskirts of troublesome French city

indicators.note: the outer letters, first and last, of the word that follows

parts.note: Nancy is a city in Lorraine

explanation.surface: Trouble on the edge of a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of a property as a tenant, the right to live in it.

clue.text: I tend new addict? About right

indicators.note: the addict goes about the right letter

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: A carer speaks of looking after a new addict.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking in the first person: someone who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurser is someone who nurses or cares for others, so the speaker who tends is one.

clue.text: Class division?

parts.note: suggests a social class, but means a sporting grouping of teams of one standard

explanation.definitionFit: A football league is a division of teams grouped by standard, a class in sporting terms.

clue.text: Benevolent philosophy in this UN aim? Drama without director unfolded

indicators.note: unfolded means opened out, so the letters spread into a new order
the play goes without its director letter

explanation.surface: A kindly creed underlying United Nations aims, and a play that has lost its director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters to rearrange. 'Drama without director' gives RAMA, which joins INTHISUNAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the doctrine of promoting human welfare, a philosophy of kindness to people.

clue.text: Delinquent blamed for uproar

indicators.note: delinquent means misbehaving, so these letters go astray from their order

explanation.surface: A young offender blamed for a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam is chaotic noise and confusion, named after a London asylum.

clue.text: Period supporting community? It's illusory

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, holding up the piece above

parts.note: a mir was a Russian peasant community
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A time when community was valued, now seen as a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: A mir was a self-governing village commune in Tsarist Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Check cinema feature?

definitions.meaning: to examine or vet, as with candidates or patients
the large surface films are projected on in a cinema

explanation.surface: Checking a film in a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to test or vet, and the screen is the projection surface in a cinema.

clue.text: Singular cunning about Gallic sage

parts.note: art can mean cunning or trickery
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A particular cleverness associated with a French wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist philosopher, a thinker from Gaul.

clue.text: Poet occupied by sick source of caricatures?

indicators.note: the poet is filled by the word for sick

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy in a Country Churchyard
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A poet consumed by illness turns satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray was an 18th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: James Gillray was a Georgian satirical cartoonist who produced many famous caricatures.

clue.text: Island captured by nationalists

indicators.note: the answer is held within the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An island seized by nationalist forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.

clue.text: Sacred works prematurely closing wartime celebration

indicators.note: the celebration stops before its last letter

parts.note: VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Holy texts cut short a wartime victory party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the ancient sacred scriptures of Hinduism.

clue.text: A nameless lucrative source for female friend abroad

indicators.note: the source of wealth loses its name letter

parts.note: a mine is a rich source of profit, as in a gold mine

explanation.surface: A rich source of money with no name, offered to a female friend overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Amie is French for a female friend, so it is the word used abroad.

clue.text: Standard road in Minnesota before part of school

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the school part
the road goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for Minnesota
the A1 is a major British road, written AI in crosswords
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability

explanation.surface: A typical main road in Minnesota leading to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, and AI is crossword shorthand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream means conventional or normal, the accepted standard.

clue.text: Chinese people following king and ruler

indicators.note: the people come after the king letter

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: Chinese subjects following their king and lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler or sovereign in central Asia, as with Genghis.

clue.text: Obtain hard chap in notice for garden

parts.note: get means obtain
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the chap is put inside the word for notice

parts.note: to see is to notice
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Getting a tough man noticed for a garden job.
explanation.definitionFit: Gethsemane is the garden outside Jerusalem where Jesus prayed before his arrest.
